basics.name: Otavio Paz Nascimento
basics.label: Electrical Engineering Student and Robotics Researcher
basics.summary: Electrical Engineering student at Columbia University with research experience in reinforcement learning, humanoid robotics, and soft robotic systems. Built and deployed a Sim2Real locomotion pipeline for the Unitree G1 using Isaac Lab and RSL-RL PPO; led independent soft robotics research under a competitive college fellowship. Demonstrated ability to work across the full research cycle: design, prototyping, testing, documentation, and dissemination. Seeking research roles in robotics, embodied AI, or related areas.

work.name: Kantaros Lab, WashU in St. Louis
work.summary: Humanoid robotics research focused on reinforcement learning and Sim2Real deployment.
highlights: Built a reinforcement learning pipeline for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot using Isaac Lab 4.5.0.
Trained a Sim2Real locomotion policy via RSL-RL PPO, achieving stable walking in under 20 hours of training.
Set up a humanoid robotics workstation: dual-boot Linux, dependency management, and deployment safety procedures.
Produced thorough technical documentation covering failures, deployment steps, and debugging procedures.

work.name: Office of Energy and Sustainability, Oberlin College
work.summary: Campus energy and water data analysis, validation, and reporting.
highlights: Analyzed campus energy and water usage via BuildingOS, managing 10+ spreadsheets across 80+ buildings.
Identified 20+ malfunctioning meters, uncovering a loss of $30,000+ for the city.
Built and documented data acquisition validation software in Python Tkinter, finding 130+ inconsistencies from 2022 to 2025.

courses: Columbia Robotics: Webmaster and RoboCONN Committee

projects.name: Design and Fabrication of Soft Robotic Actuators using Dragon Skin and Iron Powder
projects.summary: Student Researcher, Oberlin College Research Fellowship
highlights: Prototyped muscle-like actuators using Dragon Skin infused with iron powder, evaluating 5+ designs through 25+ iterations.
Reduced total fabrication cost to under $900 against a $2,000 budget, a 54% reduction through low-cost soft robotics methods.
Applied techniques in FDM 3D printing, silicone molding, and data analysis throughout design and testing.

projects.name: Renewable Energy Hybrid System at Oberlin College
highlights: Co-designed a 1.7 kW off-grid solar panel and micro wind turbine system for Shagbark Learning Center.
Secured a $3,500 grant from REpowering Schools and $1,600 from Green Edge Fund to support project implementation.
Presented at RE+ 2023 in Las Vegas and DWEA 2024, earning industry recognition.

projects.name: Papa Tick (IFSP/Salto and Biological Institute of Sao Paulo)
highlights: Developed and patented a solar-powered electric trap system, extending tick attraction duration by 80%.
Implemented firmware functionality in C, validating system performance through rigorous lab testing.
Designed the enclosure in SolidWorks 3D CAD and produced circuit diagrams for the embedded system.
